newsitem.title: USA: SBC Okla. long-distance to be rejected-WSJ.
newsitem.headline: SBC Okla. long-distance to be rejected-WSJ.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission is expected to reject SBC Communications Corp's application to offer long-distance telephone service in Oklahoma, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Tuesday's electronic edition, the Journal said FCC employees reviewing the company's application have concluded it does not qualify to enter the long-distance business yet.

If the application is rejected, it would be the first such rejection on a Baby Bell's request to offer long-distance service since last year's telecommunications law allowed local phone companies to enter the long-distance business, the Journal said.
The rejection, which has not been made final yet, could come as early as this week.
Dale Robertson, a senior vice president at SBC, spent much of Monday lobbying FCC officials on the company's position.
"It's our belief that they wouldn't let us come talk to them if they had already made a decision," he said. "So I am hopeful."
